detector._note: Keypoints 13-11-23 / 14-12-24 (elbow-shoulder-hip), vertex at the shoulder, 3D world angle. This is the angle the arm makes with the torso, not the bend of the elbow. Measured on traces/reference-shoulder-press.jsonl 6 Sep 2026: racked 53.6-55.1, locked out overhead 149.7-159.6, so a rep sweeps ~95 degrees of clear air. The elbow angle it replaced (11-13-15 / 12-14-16) only separated rack from lockout by 64 degrees and did it on the worst-observed segment: at lockout the forearm points down the camera axis, where the depth estimate is noisiest, so the same instant read 179 on one arm and 146 on the other. Under 2 cm of landmark noise the elbow config counted the clip's 3 reps correctly 25% of the time and over-counted to 4-7 the rest; this one counts 3 every time, and 92% of the time at 3 cm. The elbow-shoulder-hip angle lies in the frontal plane, which a front-framed camera sees square on, so depth barely enters it. TOP is racked at <=75, BOTTOM is locked out at >=145.

stage._note: Keypoints 13-11-23 / 14-12-24 (elbow-shoulder-hip), 3D world angle, better-seen side. Measured on the reference clip 6 Sep 2026: the rack sits at 53.6-55.1 and the weakest lockout at 149.7. Rest at <75 clears the highest rack by 20 degrees; count at >135 sits 14.7 degrees under the weakest lockout, so a press that falls short of a real lockout still counts, and 30 degrees above the lateral raise's 105 ceiling, so a raise on the same joint triple can never register as a press. The wrist-above-shoulder check is what separates a press overhead from an arm swung out behind: the angle alone cannot tell them apart, and at the counting frames the wrist measures 0.29-0.47 m above the shoulder along the torso. Ceiling 180: the arm does not go past straight in line with the torso, so a reading beyond it is a bad frame, not a bad press. The elbow floor (>70, shoulder-elbow-wrist) is enforced at the rack, the only place the joint can reach it: by the counting frame the elbow is nearly straight. On this clip the counting side's elbow never closes past 77.6, so the floor refuses none of its three reps, and the 7.6 degrees between the two is the margin. It gates the rest position rather than latching over the rep, so a single bad frame costs one frame of arming instead of a rep.

tempo._note: measured window: topExit crossing -> bottomEnter crossing, not the full descent

cues.enter: Face the camera, hands at shoulder height, upper arms down by your sides.
cues.tooHigh: Press all the way up — arms overhead, in line with your torso.
cues.tooFast: Lower the hands back to the shoulders under control.
cues.gate: Press straight up overhead, and don't drop your hands below the rack.
cues.framing: I can't see your hands — step back.
